subject.title: autoreview: secret-scanner false positives on identifier and member-expression values (e.g. `apiSecret: ctx.cloudinary.apiSecret`)

question: Should autoreview adopt language-aware safe-reference recognition for JavaScript and TypeScript while keeping non-code configuration assignments fail closed?
rationale: The false positive is established, but a global identifier exemption would alter a credential-protection boundary across multiple languages and cannot be selected safely from regex behavior alone.

options.title: Language-aware references
options.body: Recognize bounded identifier and member/index expressions only in supported code-file diff sections, with adversarial tests for unquoted config secrets.

options.title: Expand approved roots
options.body: Add ctx, environment, and similar roots to the existing allowlist, reducing immediate failures but retaining fragile name-dependent behavior.

options.title: Keep strict behavior
options.body: Retain the current scanner and document destructuring or shorthand-property workarounds, preserving security at continued workflow cost.

recommendation.title: Language-aware references
recommendation.body: Recognize bounded identifier and member/index expressions only in supported code-file diff sections, with adversarial tests for unquoted config secrets.
